text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is defined as a reading of 130/80 mm Hg or higher.

Blood pressure is recorded using two numbers: systolic (the top number, measuring pressure when the heart beats) and diastolic (the bottom number, measuring pressure when the heart rests between beats). According to guidelines from the American Heart Association, blood pressure levels are grouped into specific categories:

list.snippet: Normal: Less than 120 mm Hg systolic and less than 80 mm Hg diastolic.
Elevated: 120–129 mm Hg systolic and less than 80 mm Hg diastolic.
Stage 1 Hypertension: 130–139 mm Hg systolic or 80–89 mm Hg diastolic.
Stage 2 Hypertension: 140 mm Hg or higher systolic, or 90 mm Hg or higher diastolic.

Hypertensive Crisis: Higher than 180 mm Hg systolic and/or higher than 120 mm Hg diastolic. This requires emergency medical care, especially if accompanied by symptoms like chest pain, shortness of breath, or confusion.
